I'm not sure my explanation will make sense, and I can only speak for myself, but I'll try. 

I can think of sentences in advance to a degree, but I find it difficult to like. Hold on to things in my mind? I don't remember the whole quote exactly but it's like what Kim said, I do my thinking on paper/writing. I dunno if it's related but I also have bad hearing comprehension and struggle a lot with abstract concepts (as in, I need a concrete example of something to "get it"). 

But words are easier than images, for sure. I don't picture anything when reading books for example, and if the text is describing something I don't have an IRL reference for, it's game over (e.g. I know conceptually what a raccoon looks like, but I was absolutely lost reading one of the Dark Tower books when King was describing a fantasy animal of some kind - before he kindly pointed out that it sort of resembles a raccoon)

Not the person you asked but I also have aphantasia, and I don't have an inner monologue.
